This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.307/2023, registered at P.S.- Kanadiya District- Indore (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 506/34 of IPC.
He is in detention since 24.05.2023.
As per the prosecution story, the allegations against the applicant is that he has committed fraud with the complainants by executing an agreement regarding sale of property.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is in jail since 24.05.2023.
He has been falsely implicated.

Trial of the case will take considerable time.
It is further submitted that the applicant is aged about 75 years old and suffering from paralyses.
It is further submitted that the agreement to sale was executed by the applicant being the Attorney Holder of owner of the land but the owners of the land have not been implicated in the case.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant/accused be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant by submitting that the applicant is having strong criminal record of six cases of similar nature.

Counsel for the objector has also opposed the prayer by stating that the applicant has committed forgery with the complainant and other persons and taken the amount of Rs.8,35,000/- and prays for return of the amount.

In response to the aforesaid submissions, counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is not in a position to deposit whole amount, but one month time may be granted to him for deposition of 50% of the amount.
In this case, after investigation, charge sheet has been filed.

Therefore, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the rival submissions made by counsel for the parties, the application is allowed and the applicant shall be released on bail subject to deposit 50% of the amount i.e.
Rs.4,17,500/- in the account of the complainant Rajesh Solanki within a period of 30 days from today and on his further furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
It is also made clear that if the applicant fail to deposit the aforesaid amount, this order shall stands cancelled automatically without further reference to this Court.
The counsel for the complainant shall provide the bank account details to the counsel for the applicant within two days.
The learned trial Court is also directed to release the applicant on bail subject to verification of fulfillment of the aforesaid condition.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
